photo.description: Vines and a green valley with distant hills framed by two umbrella pines; location confirmed on Unsplash as Abruzzo (exact town not stated)

regions.notes: Share: the consortium says Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC 'da solo, rappresenta oltre l'80% del totale dei vini a denominazione prodotti in Abruzzo'. That is a share of DO wines, not all wine, and treating it as 'red' is an inference: the page doesn't use the word rosso, but Cerasuolo is now a separate rosé DOC, so Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC is red only. Wine Folly also says 'Look for red wines'. Drop main/share if that inference isn't acceptable. Controguerra passito and spumante exist but are minor, so Sweet and Sparkling are left out.

photo.description: Limestone cliffs and autumn woods of the Baume-les-Messieurs reculée, with the village on the valley floor; caption: Baume-les-Messieurs, Jura, autumn 2019 (no vines in frame; the village sits in the Côtes du Jura area)

regions.notes: Shares are 'répartition des ventes par produit' in hectolitres, Aug 2022 to Jul 2023 (CIVJ 2024 key-figures infographic, p.2): rouge 19%, blanc 42%, vin jaune 4%, crémant 29%, macvin 6%, vin de paille 1%. Vin Jaune (4%) is a dry flor-aged white listed separately from 'blanc', so white is 42% (46% with vin jaune). Sweet = Macvin (fortified) 6% + vin de paille 1%. main is set because white is the largest share stated. No confirmed Jura vineyard photo on Unsplash.
